correctness.rationale: Weighted Matrix–Tree cofactor evaluation gives the all-vertex excess-degree probability-generating polynomial. This factors into independent categorical occupancy trials. Conditioning on one trial proves the exact local mixed covariance; row-sum cancellation yields the weighted-Laplacian identity. The leaf probability increases strictly with part size, all pair weights are strictly positive for at least three parts, and a separate bipartite factorization handles stars and all other boundary cases. Exhaustive ordinary Prüfer enumeration and exact rational arithmetic confirm the formula for eight small multipartite graphs (up to seven vertices), and a larger parameter grid confirms the signs, 165 checks in total. The universal result is analytical rather than based on finite tests.

value.rationale: The mixed dependence of a local tree degree on the global number of leaves is a natural question in nonhomogeneous random spanning trees. An exact positive-weight Laplacian identity converts every such covariance into differences of leaf probabilities. It gives a complete unconditional sign classification for smallest and largest multipartite classes (and exact neutral bipartite and balanced boundaries), while intermediate classes can exhibit opposite signs at nearby natural part-size triples. This is a structural finite-family theorem, not merely a recomputation of spanning-tree counts or a new finite table.
